learning: Pending the race. If line_loss_events fall to zero but max_error stays near 0.06 m, the limit is steering response, not visibility. If line loss persists, the spread or footprint is still too narrow.
notes: Widened ±0.03 m spread with sensor weights scaled to x/0.02 so steering gain matches iteration 0. Gains unchanged to isolate the spread effect.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the symmetric five-sensor baseline at x = ±0.02 m. All 60 trials ended off track with one line-loss event each, max_error about 0.061 m, and progress of only 0.035 to 0.115. The Builder's iteration-1 geometry widens the spread to x = ±0.03 m (5 sensors, 12 mm footprint, y = 0.05 m) and keeps body, wheel, and mass fixed. I built the controller for that exact geometry. Sensor weights are scaled to x/0.02 (-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5). This keeps the signal gain per metre of lateral offset the same as the iteration-0 controller (kp 2.0 and weights of ±1 at 0.02 m), so the race isolates the spread change and does not confound it with a gain change. The weights stay within the ±2 limit. Gains are otherwise unchanged (base_speed 1.6, ki 0, kd 0.05, line_loss last_direction). I did not raise kp or kd yet, because iteration 0 gave no evidence about whether steering or line recovery is the limit, and changing both would hide the spread effect. The observation request keeps the full measurement set, so the next feedback can separate line loss, drift, and oscillation.
